newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Apr 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Apr 30.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- Beijing plans to re-arrange quotas given to different provinces for people to emigrate to Hong Kong, giving priority to Guangdong which has closer ties with the territory.
-- APPLE DAILY -- Mainland police cracked down on a gang in Guangzhou and Wuhan involved in forging one-way permits and selling them to people who wanted to move to Hong Kong.

-- SING TAO DAILY -- Beijing has told ministries and provincial governments not to contact future Hong Kong chief executive Tung Chee-hwa directly. It said requests for meetings between Tung and ministerial and provincial leaders would be handled by the Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office after July 1.

-- WEN WEI PO -- The leaders of both British parties, John Major and Tony Blair, said they paid high attention to Britain's relations with China. Blair expressed hope Hong Kong would be a bridge linking the two nations, instead of an aruging point.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese Vice-Premier Qian Qichen explained the concept of "one country two systems" to his U.S. counterparts and said China would ensure a peaceful Hong Kong handover which would be in the interests of all countries.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa said there would be no brutal suppression of demonstrations in the territory after the handover like the 1989 crackdown on pro-democracy demonstrators in Tiananmen Square.

-- The full effects of a two-year regulatory blitz on leveraged foreign exchange dealers has started to hit home, with dealers reporting profits severely undermined by stringent rules on margin requirements and keen competition from retail banks.
